arguments.body:
MEMORANDUM

TO: Engagement Team — Funds Asset Management
FROM: Core Operations — Redline Review
DATE: [Current Date]
RE: Redline Review Memorandum — Investment Advisory Agreement
MATTER: Matter File 15 — Funds Asset Management
ENGAGEMENT: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Investment Advisory Agreement

--------------------------------------------------------------------
I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
This memorandum summarizes our comprehensive review of the redlined
investment advisory agreement against the firm's standard form and the
internal playbook. The review focuses on the counterparty's latest markup
and identifies each deviation from firm precedent, assesses its market
reasonableness, and recommends a negotiating position. The analysis is
grounded in the operative record in Matter File 15 and the applicable
regulatory framework governing investment advisers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The counterparty's markup introduces a series of changes across the
representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing,
indemnification, and termination provisions. Most changes are consistent
with market practice for institutional investment advisory agreements;
however, several provisions require pushback to protect the adviser's
fiduciary posture and limit uncapped or open-ended liability. The most
significant items are the proposed expansion of the indemnification scope,
the narrowing of the adviser's standard of care, and the addition of
unilateral termination rights in favor of the client.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
III. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A. Standard Form Position
The standard form contains customary representations and warranties
concerning the adviser's registration status, authority to enter the
agreement, absence of conflicts, and accuracy of the Form ADV disclosure.

B. Counterparty Markup
The counterparty has (i) added a representation that the adviser will
maintain a specified minimum level of errors-and-omissions insurance
throughout the term, (ii) broadened the accuracy representation to cover
all marketing materials and performance data, and (iii) added a
representation that the adviser's compliance program complies with Rule
206(4)-7 under the Advisers Act.

C. Assessment
The insurance and compliance-program representations are reasonable and
consistent with institutional market practice. The expansion of the
accuracy representation to all marketing materials and performance data
is broader than the standard form and should be narrowed to material
information and to materials provided to the client in connection with
the engagement.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. COVENANTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A. Standard Form Position
The standard form includes covenants regarding compliance with applicable
law, maintenance of registration, prompt notification of material
changes, and cooperation in regulatory examinations.

B. Counterparty Markup
The counterparty has added (i) a covenant requiring the adviser to
provide advance notice of any change in key personnel, (ii) a covenant
requiring the adviser to maintain and enforce a business continuity plan,
and (iii) a covenant requiring the adviser to provide the client with
access to its books and records upon reasonable notice.

C. Assessment
The key-personnel notice and business-continuity covenants are market
standard and acceptable. The books-and-records access covenant should be
limited to records relating to the client's account and to reasonable
business hours, consistent with the adviser's obligations under the
Advisers Act.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
V. CONDITIONS TO CLOSING
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A. Standard Form Position
The standard form conditions closing on the execution of the agreement,
delivery of the Form ADV, and the absence of any material adverse change.

B. Counterparty Markup
The counterparty has added a condition requiring the adviser to deliver
a certificate of insurance evidencing the minimum coverage levels, and a
condition that no regulatory proceeding be pending or threatened against
the adviser.

C. Assessment
The certificate-of-insurance condition is reasonable. The regulatory-
proceeding condition is broader than market practice and should be
narrowed to proceedings that would reasonably be expected to have a
material adverse effect on the adviser's ability to perform.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. INDEMNIFICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A. Standard Form Position
The standard form provides for mutual indemnification for losses arising
from each party's breach of the agreement, negligence, or willful
misconduct, with customary carve-outs.

B. Counterparty Markup
The counterparty's markup materially expands the adviser's indemnification
obligation by (i) removing the negligence/willful-misconduct qualifier and
imposing a broader "any act or omission" standard, (ii) adding an
indemnification for third-party claims arising from the adviser's
investment decisions regardless of fault, and (iii) removing the
limitation-of-liability cap.

C. Assessment — HIGH PRIORITY
These changes are the most significant deviations and are not market
standard. We recommend the following:
  - Restore the negligence/willful-misconduct qualifier and reject the
    "any act or omission" standard.
  - Reject indemnification for investment decisions absent a finding of
    negligence, breach, or willful misconduct.
  - Reinstate a limitation-of-liability provision, typically capped at
    the aggregate fees paid under the agreement, with carve-outs for
    fraud, willful misconduct, and breaches of confidentiality.
This is a key negotiating priority and should not be conceded.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. TERMINATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A. Standard Form Position
The standard form provides for termination for cause, upon material
breach, and for convenience upon advance written notice.

B. Counterparty Markup
The counterparty has added (i) a right to terminate immediately upon the
adviser's loss of registration or regulatory sanction, and (ii) a right
to terminate for convenience on shortened notice without payment of
accrued fees.

C. Assessment
The immediate-termination right upon loss of registration or regulatory
sanction is reasonable and market standard. The shortened convenience
notice and the elimination of accrued-fee payment should be resisted;
termination for convenience should require reasonable notice and payment
of fees accrued through the effective termination date.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
VIII. REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The agreement must remain consistent with the adviser's fiduciary duties
under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, including the duty of care and
loyalty. The proposed expansion of the indemnification scope and the
narrowing of the standard of care should be evaluated to ensure they do
not conflict with the adviser's regulatory obligations or create
disclosures required under Form ADV Part 2A. Any performance-related
representations must be consistent with the SEC's marketing rule under
Rule 206(4)-1.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
IX. RECOMMENDATIONS AND NEXT STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Push back on the expanded indemnification scope and the removal of the
   limitation-of-liability cap (highest priority).
2. Narrow the accuracy representation to material information and
   engagement-related materials.
3. Limit the books-and-records access covenant to client-account records.
4. Narrow the regulatory-proceeding condition to material adverse effect.
5. Resist shortened convenience termination and require payment of accrued
   fees.
6. Confirm all changes are consistent with the adviser's fiduciary duties
   and Form ADV disclosure obligations.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
X. CONCLUSION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The counterparty's markup is largely consistent with institutional market
practice, but several provisions require negotiation to protect the
adviser's position. The indemnification and limitation-of-liability
changes are the highest-priority items and should be addressed before
execution. We recommend engaging opposing counsel on the items identified
above and updating the internal playbook to reflect any agreed deviations.

Prepared by: Core Operations — Funds Asset Management
Matter File 15

- **Representations & warranties** — flags the counterparty's additions (insurance minimums, broadened accuracy rep, Rule 206(4)-7 compliance) and recommends narrowing the accuracy rep to material, engagement-related information.

- **Regulatory considerations** — ties changes to fiduciary duties under the Advisers Act, Form ADV Part 2A, and the SEC marketing rule.
